requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) is configured as the DNS resolver on the shared private network (10.100.206.0/24)
requirements.summary: PowerDNS Recursor on node1 was configured to listen on 10.100.206.10 with allow-from 10.100.206.0/24, committed and saved (cmd-297c09061348422f). Post-restart, the recursor is active and listening on that address (after_executor listening-sockets shows udp/tcp 10.100.206.10:53 owned by pdns_recursor), confirming the config persisted.

requirements.requirement: node1 answers queries for inventory.internal with node2's address (10.100.206.11)
requirements.summary: A static-host-mapping (inventory.internal -> 10.100.206.11) was committed and saved on node1; dig @10.100.206.10 inventory.internal returns 10.100.206.11 both immediately after configuration and again after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other DNS queries upstream (to the platform gateway/upstream resolver)
requirements.summary: dig @10.100.206.10 example.com returns real public IPs both before and after node1's reboot, confirming forwarding to the configured upstream name-server (10.100.206.1).

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 are configured to resolve through node1
requirements.summary: nmcli set ipv4.dns=10.100.206.10 with ipv4.ignore-auto-dns=yes on both nodes; /etc/resolv.conf shows nameserver 10.100.206.10 on both; getent hosts resolves inventory.internal to 10.100.206.11 and example.com externally on both nodes, both immediately and after each node's reboot (confirming the NetworkManager connection profile change persisted).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node1 (VyOS) runs PowerDNS Recursor bound to the shared LAN address, answers inventory.internal with node2's address via a static-host-mapping, and forwards all other queries to the upstream gateway; node2 and node3 are configured via NetworkManager to use node1 as their sole DNS resolver. Behavior was verified both before and after a full one-at-a-time reboot of all three nodes, with distinct pre/post boot_ids and recovered service/config/resolution state on every node, giving strong confidence the configuration is persistent and not just transiently applied. The only notable hygiene issue is a reverted mid-task experiment (authoritative-domain zone approach) that was fully superseded by the final static-host-mapping approach with no residue.
limitations: Restart/reboot evidence, while not itself a stated task requirement, was executed per the mandatory provider-wide protocol and is coherent: pre-restart boot_id/health, restart acknowledgement, distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered DNS service/config/resolution are all directly observed on node1, node2, and node3, matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots.

Command exit code 3 on cmd-b313789ee883422e (pdns-recursor 'inactive') and the transient connection-timeout/reset errors during each reboot are expected artifacts of the pre-configuration baseline and the reboot process itself, not evidence of failure.

operational_hygiene.summary: One bounded troubleshooting mutation was made and then reverted: the executor first configured node1's DNS forwarding using the VyOS 'authoritative-domain' zone approach (cmd-80ef6eb0284d4231, committed+saved), which turned out to return NXDOMAIN instead of resolving inventory.internal. This was undone in the final working configuration (cmd-297c09061348422f, which deletes 'authoritative-domain' and switches to a static-host-mapping) — an intermediate 'delete name-server' commit (cmd-239d3cbd8da64f78) was also part of this troubleshooting and was superseded. Both mutations were committed to the persistent VyOS config at the time but were fully reverted/superseded before the task concluded, so no residue remains (after_executor shows no failed services, no leftover authoritative-domain zone config, and only expected systemd-private/reboot.log temp artifacts). All other state-changing commands (dns forwarding setup, static-host-mapping, nmcli DNS changes, and the three node reboots) map directly to satisfying task requirements or the mandated restart-evidence protocol.
